data.body:
Audit findings from task 7be3-69af-6e84-4235 (the two decoupled wins split out of this consolidation). Recording them here so the consolidation design has the evidence base.

## Capability matrix — the three commands are cleanly disjoint today

| command | reads | checks | can mutate |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fsck` | raw event bytes + git refs | store integrity: log/snapshot/ref consistency, orphans | yes (`--repair`, `--dry-run`, `--limit`, `--repair-snapshots`) |
| `validate` | reduced ticket semantics | repo-wide tracker health score 1-5, bucketed critical/major/minor/warning | no |
| `doctor` | link graph + store diagnostics | link/store diagnostic surface, incl. blocking-link audit under older rules | yes (`--repair`, `--dry-run`) |

`fsck` reads bytes; `validate` reads reduced semantics. There is no overlap in what they inspect, so "which one confirms store integrity" has exactly one answer (`fsck`) — which is what made the doc bug below a real misdirection rather than a style nit.

## `validate --fix` was advertised and did nothing

`_engine_support/validate.py` carried `elif arg == "--fix": pass  # accepted, no-op (the bash --fix path is unimplemented)`. It was advertised at SIX independent sites (the in-file `_HELP` usage line and option description, the two runtime "Run with --fix to attempt automatic repairs (interactive)" hints, `_cli/help/validate.txt`, `_cli/help/overview.txt`, `README.md`, and the generated `docs/cli-reference.md`) — and a user following the tool's own printed remedy got silence. Maintainer decision was REMOVE, not implement: `doctor` is the fixing path. Removed under 7be3; `--fix` now falls through validate's existing unknown-option handler (`Unknown option: --fix`, exit 1), and both runtime hints now point at `rebar doctor`.

Note for the consolidation: the under-enumeration of that edit set blocked plan review four times. Any consolidation that moves or renames a flag should treat `grep -rn -- '<flag>' src/ docs/ README.md` as the enumeration method, not a curated list — the generated `docs/cli-reference.md` and the two separate help sources (in-file `_HELP` vs packaged `_cli/help/*.txt`) are easy to miss independently.

## `doctor` is invoked by nothing

`rebar doctor` is dispatched only from `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:323`. Outside the CLI dispatch plus its own help text and generated reference, the only mentions in the repo are prose: `CHANGELOG.md` (the entry announcing it) and `docs/ticket-model.md` (two lines describing the blocking-link audit). No script, CI workflow, Makefile target, agent skill, or AGENTS.md/CONTRIBUTING guidance ever tells anyone to run it. So the command the project designates as "the path for fixing" has no adoption surface at all — that gap is arguably more load-bearing for this consolidation than the naming overlap.

## Wrong-command doc, fixed

`docs/chatgpt-agent-guide.md` told agents to run "`rebar validate` (or `rebar fsck`) against the tracker to confirm store integrity". Store integrity is not something `validate` inspects. Corrected under 7be3 to name `fsck`, with a parenthetical stating the split. Prior evidence that this ambiguity costs real work: epics `dabb` and `18ae-4f54-a85b-4ddb` were independently filed scoping the same `doctor` command, and `18ae` was closed as a duplicate.
